One surface was declaring that nine inputs are rechecked at read time on behalf of three operations, one of which has no viewer to recheck four of them against. The split does not weaken the rule; it states which half of it getGlobalLeaderboard can actually run, which is what stops a reader inferring from the surface list that a block is enforced there.

The figures come from a sealed generation and the authorization does not. That separation is what lets a block change what a viewer sees without changing what was sealed. Every friend, rival and board view is served here and every input applies to at least one of them.

profiles.presence_visibility exists as a separate column precisely because the two policies are separate: a public profile with private presence is a state the product supports, and folding one into the other would remove the setting.

Presence is device activity, not standing. A retired or restricted identity that is still signed in is still online to the people it authorized, and suppressing that would announce the sanction D-084 keeps private.

surfaces.note: The one snapshot-time surface, and the only one no API response renders: the package is delivered by a download grant rather than a JSON body, which is why it is reachable from derived_artifacts rather than from boundaries. account-lifecycle is not vacuous here — deletion-pending revokes the grant, which is the PF-028 revocation route.

derived_artifacts.invalidation: The cursor pins authorization_revision at issue. A presentation whose current revision differs is refused authorization-revision-moved and the client starts the page again. Nothing is deleted: the server stores no cursor, so invalidation is a comparison rather than a write, and that is why the revision has to be inside the signed record.
derived_artifacts.note: conformance/planning/ranking-cursor-vectors-v1.json already exercises the refusal. What was missing is the statement of which changes reach it, which is what the trigger table now computes.

derived_artifacts.invalidation: revoked_at is set, after which the grant_digest no longer admits a download. The row survives for the audit trail; the capability does not. This is the PF-028 revocation route, and account-lifecycle is the only input that reaches it because the subject and the viewer of an export are the same person.
derived_artifacts.note: A grant is the one derived artifact that is a server row, so it is the one that can be revoked rather than only refused.

derived_artifacts.invalidation: There is nothing to invalidate, and that is the point: every operation that is not universally public is declared no-store, so no shared cache, proxy or CDN ever holds a response whose authorization could go stale. A cache entry cannot be invalidated by a block it never hears about, so the policy is the invalidation. Before PF-033 the document declared no cache directive at all, which left a viewer-relative profile response storable by any intermediary.
derived_artifacts.note: Only the universally-public reference and global-board operations are shared-cacheable, and that set is derived from x-public-operations rather than listed twice.

derived_artifacts.invalidation: Never invalidated by an authorization change, and recorded here so that the exemption is stated rather than inferred from an absence. A sealed generation holds figures and positions and carries no handle, no viewer and no authorization state, so a block changes what renders from it and not what it contains. This is the line SR-015 turns on: an immutable historical fact and a current authorization are two records precisely so that changing the second never has to rewrite the first.
derived_artifacts.note: It is also the only projection the evaluation permits caching, because it is identical for every viewer.

invalidation_triggers.note: blocks.established_at advances. Deny-hard, so it reaches every surface that evaluates it, and it reaches the cursor because the cursor pinned a revision that has now moved.
Removing a block restores visibility because nothing was destroyed; the revision still moves, so a cursor issued while the block held is still refused rather than silently widened.

board_memberships.revision and the board-scoped boards.membership_revision advance in the same transaction. A removed member's board leaderboard cursor stops resolving; their sealed entries do not move.
boards.state leaves active. Membership of an archived board is history rather than current authorization, so the widen stops.
friend_edges.established_at advances. An ended friendship and a block are two changes and not one, which is why they are two triggers.
rival_edges has no revision column, so the state is the change signal; it detects a change and cannot order two, which is a limitation of the input rather than of the trigger.
profiles.updated_at advances. Narrowing is retroactive on live surfaces and not on sealed generations.
profiles.presence_visibility changes. The lease keeps transitioning; the projection collapses to offline, which is the same value an inactive participant reads.

accounts.state becomes deletion-pending. This is the widest trigger: account-lifecycle is deny-hard and subject-only, so it is the one input every surface evaluates, and therefore the one trigger that reaches the export download grant.

ranked_identities.revision advances. A retired identity stops being projected; a restricted one still appears with its credited figure, because hiding the entry would announce a sanction D-084 keeps private.

evaluation.note: Nothing here is implemented. This is the rule an implementation is measured against, and no surface in this repository evaluates it. What PF-033 changed is that the rule is now total over the API: every operation in openapi-v1.yaml has a boundary, every third-party boundary has a surface, every surface answers for all nine inputs, and every viewer-visible field carries the revision set that gates it. An unimplemented rule that is total is checkable against the document it governs; one that is partial is not, because the part it omits and the part nobody thought of look the same.
